title: Donovan Mitchell Record Best Scoring Game in Win Over Sixers and Phillie Fans Has That One Kid in 2k to Blame for Cavs Star's Crazy Night - NewsBreak
text:
By Rolly Gacelo ,
22 minutes ago Donovan Mitchell record his best game so far of the season after sending the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 132-121 win over the Philadelphia 76ers with his 46 points on 71.4 percent shooting. It is the Cavs fifth win in eight games.
Nov 2, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) reacts against the Atlanta Hawks during the second half at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images The Cavs are already motivated to do better than the last season when the fell in the second round as a top seed in the Eastern Conference. Mitchell will not run out of reason to perform better and this game against the Sixers was more personal.
Talking to reporters post game, the six-time All-Star credited a heckler he met in 2k video game for his explosive game.
“This kid pissed me off today. I was playing 2K. I told him too I was like wait just wait,” he said.
“And he just called me washed up, he called me a bunch of things but I love it. He saying he ain’t seen a highlight from me in a minute and I just told him alright we’ll see. This game was for that kid or grown man whoever that was so I appreciate you. I told him I’d give him a shoutout too.”
Nov 5, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (45) brings the ball up court in the third quarter against the Philadelphia 76ers at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Donovan Mitchell, Cavs bigs delivered This is the Cavs second straight win after losing to the Toronto Raptors in a game where they were much favored.
Mitchell had help despite his dominance in the game. Jarrett Allen made a triumphant return after missing the last two games, scoring 24 points and grabbing 10 rebounds. He was also a menace on the defensive end with his three steals and three blocks.
Nov 5, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Philadelphia 76ers center Andre Drummond (1) and Cleveland Cavaliers center Jarrett Allen (31) reacts in the first quarter at Rocket Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Evan Mobley continued his double digit scoring by contributing 23. Huge and consistent from the bench was Sam Merrill who had 13.
As for the Sixers, they played without Joel Embiid and Paul George. This is their second straight defeat after bowing to the Chicago Bulls the other on a buzzer beating 3-point shot by Nikola Vucevic.
